name: Le casier de tri
camera: close view of the tall oak sorting cabinet at the BACK CENTRE of the hall, same tiles and plank floor

setting.walls: the same off-white plaster above the white-and-cornflower-blue tiles
setting.floor: the same pale grey-washed oak boards
setting.landmark: the tall honey-oak sorting cabinet of pigeonholes
setting.style: B15 La Poste: warm playful storybook painterly 3.5/5, cool neutral daylight

painted_way_out.painted_as: the plank floor in the near foreground
painted_way_out.control: strip hierarchy Back (gate 8: no second button to the same place)

note: Five feminine nouns and one adjective (postal, far left by the post box); single-gender zoom, so no divider. Repainted 08:40 (track S07->S06): six separated groups, distinct characters, cool daylight.

items.scene: A TALL ("TAHL") young giraffe holds her letter in her mouth to post it into the yellow POSTAL box.
A red squirrel in a blue postman's cap stands on a stepladder for the DISTRIBUTION ("dees-TREE-bew-SYOHN"), tucking one letter into each pigeonhole like nuts into TREE holes.
A grey owl in a waistcoat sorts letters into a tray of wooden PARTITIONS ("ray-pahr-tee-SYOHN"): the ALLOCATION of the morning mail.
A bearded delivery man in brown overalls wheels in a hand-truck with a crate of giant purple RAISINS to LEAVE: a DELIVERY ("lee-vreh-ZOHN").
A grey-haired postwoman kneels for the HANDOVER of a small parcel to three MICE ("ruh-MEEZ") waiting on the floor.
A young woman gardener in a straw hat opens her PARCEL ("pahr-SEHL") box to show a PLOT OF LAND inside: a tiny square of lawn with one daisy.
